concepts.def: Daily routine vocabulary describing what you do each day, often using reflexive verbs like 'se lever' and 'se coucher'.
Reflexive verbs such as 'se laver' and 'se brosser les dents', used for daily actions and taking 'être' in the perfect tense.
School-day vocabulary: lessons, timetable, subjects and getting to school, common in everyday-activity topics.
Meals and food: 'le petit-déjeuner', 'le déjeuner' and 'le dîner', plus typical foods eaten during the day.
Shopping for everyday needs, including food shops and asking for items and prices.
Telling the time, essential for describing when daily activities happen, e.g. 'à sept heures et demie'.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Area A: Everyday Activities — a core area of GCSE French.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Area A: Everyday Activities brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Area A: Everyday Activities.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which sentence correctly says 'I get up at seven o'clock'?
options: Je me lève à sept heures.
Je lève à sept heures.
Je me lever sept heures.
Je suis sept heures.

mcqs.q: 'Se brosser les dents' is an example of which type of verb?
options: A reflexive (pronominal) verb
An adjective
A preposition
A noun
Breakfast
Dinner
A small park
Lunchbox

mcqs.q: How do you say 'half past seven'?
options: sept heures et demie
sept heures et quart
huit heures moins le quart
six heures et demie

mcqs.q: How do you say 'I get up' using a reflexive verb?
options: Je lève
Je me lève
Je suis lever
aller

mcqs.q: Which auxiliary do reflexive verbs take in the perfect tense?
options: Je suis lever
être
avoir
aller
